stories.headline: Ferragamo Declines in the third Quarter
stories.claim: Ferragamo's third-quarter revenue fell 3.5% to €207 million as wholesale declined and China slowed.
stories.summary: Salvatore Ferragamo reported third-quarter 2026 revenue down 3.5% year on year to €207 million, which it blamed on geopolitical unrest and weaker summer demand. Revenue for the first nine months was flat at €675 million, with a 19.1% fall in wholesale offsetting direct-to-consumer results. Direct-to-consumer sales were flat in the quarter, with North America and Europe strong and Asia, particularly China, still slowing. The company plans to close some stores in lower-tier Chinese cities and expand e-commerce, while creative director Maximilian Davis's shows are being turned into store sales. The turnaround is expected to be gradual.

stories.headline: Tighter rules planned to protect people from cosmetic surgery that goes badly wrong
stories.claim: UK government plans tighter rules so only trained professionals can offer high-risk cosmetic procedures, with a ban for under-18s.
stories.summary: The government has set out plans for England to restrict high-risk non-surgical cosmetic procedures, including liquid Brazilian butt lifts, vampire facials and deep chemical peels, to properly trained professionals from 2027. Liquid BBLs would be legally classed as cosmetic surgery so only doctors could perform them. High-risk procedures for under-18s would be banned, and rogue providers would face new criminal offences and fixed fines of up to £4,000. The draft rules now go to consultation before parliament considers them in spring 2027. Health Minister Karin Smyth said the aim was to drive rogue operators out of the market.

The filing also shifts several routes between A340-300, 787-9, A350-900 and 747-400 aircraft, with some frequencies increased or reduced. stories.summary: Preliminary results show more than two-thirds of Alberta voters chose to remain in Canada in Monday's referendum on separation, a result Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed as strengthening his hand. The vote came as Canada faces a trade war with the United States, and Carney is pushing diversification, major infrastructure projects and a proposed pipeline to the Pacific that would reduce dependence on the US. Separatist leaders had reportedly met US State Department officials in Washington to discuss an independent Alberta. Nine other referendum questions, covering provincial powers and immigration, still have implications for the country. Carney remains popular in polls, including in Alberta.

He built it around an imagined atlas of everyday references such as prickly pears, braids, aprons and Papantla hats, translated into tailoring, pleats, headpieces and volumes rather than literal motifs. The review argues it may be his strongest collection so far, balancing conceptual narrative with commercially appealing clothes.

stories.headline: Italy approves sweeping security measures in response to protests
stories.claim: Italy's cabinet approved 500 troops for Milan and tougher protest penalties after weekend cost-of-living unrest.
stories.summary: Italy's cabinet approved sending 500 troops to Milan and new legal measures after cost-of-living protests turned violent in northern cities at the weekend. The new offence covers taking part in a group of at least five people who endanger public safety, with up to five years in prison and fines of up to €20,000. Parents can be held liable for vandalism by minors, and police can detain 14 to 17-year-olds who pose a danger. The cabinet did not approve giving soldiers policing powers, after opposition from President Mattarella. Protests were driven by fuel and energy prices, rents and wages, and a separate lorry-driver protest in the south is disrupting supply chains. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni faces pressure ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.claim: Four Gemini 4 agents completed Minecraft's Ender Dragon fight autonomously, per a Google research paper.

stories.claim: UN biodiversity summit Cop17 opens in Yerevan to assess progress on 2030 nature targets, which are largely off track.
stories.summary: The UN Convention on Biological Diversity's Cop17 summit takes place in Yerevan, Armenia, from 19 to 30 October, where governments will assess progress on the 23 targets agreed in Montreal in 2022. Countries have acknowledged they are off track on every target, though 27.5% of land is close to the 30% protection goal. Progress on reforming $500bn of environmentally damaging subsidies is almost nil, and the Cali Fund for private contributions has received only $10,656 in commitments. Funding cuts by the US and European countries add to the challenge, and negotiators face a crowded agenda after the previous Cop16 ended in disarray.

stories.summary: Victoria Police say independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was struck by a white Toyota outside an office on Murphy Street in Wangaratta at about 3.35pm local time. A 43-year-old Tarrawingee man was arrested at the scene, reportedly by a passer-by, and a knife was seized from the vehicle. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described it as a deliberate act, while the opposition leader and state premier condemned the attack. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said reported threats and harassment against politicians rose from 951 to 1,067 in the past year. Counterterrorism and major investigation detectives are involved, and police have not yet confirmed whether the parties knew each other.

stories.claim: A cybersecurity expert assesses how realistic Bill Gates' warning of AI causing a billion deaths is.
stories.summary: Tom's Guide interviewed David Linthicum, a cloud, AI and cybersecurity consultant, about Bill Gates' warning that AI could cause a billion deaths. Linthicum argues that a superintelligent AI wiping out humanity remains largely hypothetical, since it would need control over critical infrastructure, weapons and biological systems without human intervention. He says the more immediate risks are fraud, deepfakes, data leakage and poorly engineered AI connected to business and government systems. He recommends least-privilege access, human approval for high-risk actions, monitoring and basic defences such as multifactor authentication. He also judges that AI-enabled biological weapons are speculative given the practical barriers.
key_points: The article gathers an expert view on Bill Gates' warning that AI could cause a billion deaths.

Brands including McQueen, Ferragamo and Miu Miu featured some curve models, but the overall trend showed regression. London ranked as the most inclusive city, helped by Chopova Lowena, while Milan ranked lowest. The report links the decline to GLP-1 discourse, heroin-chic aesthetics and conservatism in fashion.

Total curve representation of 2.5% has almost halved from 5.1% for FW25.
London was the most size-inclusive city, while Milan had just 0.1% plus-size looks.

Experts link the decline to GLP-1 discourse, heroin-chic trends and conservatism.
